purpose: Read-only live retrieval quality probe against the deployed HokieHelp stack (embeddings-service + Qdrant). Descriptive only — no invented ground truth; credit totals are NOT judged.

environment.embedding_model: BAAI/bge-m3 (per embeddings-config configmap; verified by re-embedding stored chunks at cosine 1.000000)
environment.query_prefix: none (raw query text, matching live chatbot)

parameters.production_diff: prod uses candidates=50, top_k=8; version partition is a no-op on this collection (no edition payload fields present)

embedding_compatibility.verified_model: BAAI/bge-m3 (configmap embeddings-config BGE_MODEL) — dense 1024-d + sparse lexical weights, served by embeddings-service POST /embed and POST /rerank (bge-reranker-v2-m3)
embedding_compatibility.verification: Re-embedded compose_embed_text(title, headings, body) of live points via the service and compared to their stored dense vectors: cosine 1.000000 / 0.999996. Body-only text scores 0.944-0.971, confirming corpus vectors are identity-composed (embed_version=2), matching the live ingestor.
embedding_compatibility.query_encoding: Live chatbot embeds the RAW query text via the embeddings-service — no 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:' prefix.
checkout_mismatches: Branch retriever.py builds SentenceTransformer(EMBEDDING_MODEL, default 'BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5') locally and prepends BGE_QUERY_PREFIX — different model family AND different query convention than the live corpus.
Its query_points call omits using='dense'; against hokiehelp-test (named vectors) it fails with HTTP 400 'Not existing vector name error' (reproduced read-only).

Its collection default is 'hokiehelp_chunks' (live chatbot uses 'hokiehelp-test') and its min_score=0.53 is a bge-large cosine heuristic — live thresholding uses raw cross-encoder rerank scores with floor 0.3.
Its adjacent-chunk expansion parses chunk_id by rsplit('_', 1) expecting '{hash}_{seq:04d}'; live ids are '{hash}#{seq:04d}', so neighbor expansion silently no-ops.
Both bge-large-en-v1.5 and bge-m3 are 1024-dim, so a naive port would NOT fail on dimension — it would silently query a mismatched vector space.
embedding_compatibility.conclusion: Branch retrieval code must target BAAI/bge-m3 through the embeddings-service (or any client producing byte-identical vectors) and use using='dense' with the server-side sparse+RRF fusion. No reindex or model change is required or approved — the live corpus and embeddings-service are already mutually consistent.

findings: GitHub #29 exact regression reproduced: 'how many credits do i need to graduate BS in CS' ranks Data-Centric Computing and Secure Computing governance 'Supporting Docs' (2019-2020 proposal PDFs) at ranks 1-2 (rerank 0.978/0.977) above every CS checksheet. The failure originates at the dense stage (top-1 cosine 0.7189) and survives rerank.

Same query family diverges wildly: github29-p1 top-1 is the correct coe_cs_23_24 checksheet (wrong-program docs at ranks 2/4); github29-p3 returns five CS checksheets spanning four different years; the normalized phrasing returns graduate MS/PhD degree pages at ranks 1-2/4-5 (degree-level confusion).

Paraphrase consistency is poor: ZERO canonical URLs are shared across all six CS-intent variants; pairwise top-5 URL Jaccard ranges 0.000-0.429. Same-intent paraphrases retrieve materially different source sets.
Rerank score compression: right-program and wrong-program documents both score 0.96-0.99, so rerank score alone cannot separate them; the 0.3 floor only separates out-of-corpus entities.

Unknown-entity behaviour is clean: fictional faculty name max rerank 0.0575, fictional program 0.0184 — both far below the 0.3 floor (0 selected); lowest real-query top-1 in this suite was 0.5979. No abstention grey zone between ~0.06 and ~0.60 was observed.

GitHub #16 followups: raw 'What math courses does it require?' (history: CS major) retrieves MATH-department documents exclusively (MathMajorHandbook top-1, 0.9525); the context-composed variant retrieves CS pages. Pronoun-only 'What courses do they teach?' returns just 4 above-floor chunks with an Entomology page top-1 (0.5979). Context resolution must happen BEFORE retrieval.

University-scope failures: 'What are the admission requirements for Virginia Tech?' top-1 is Geography GRADUATE programs (0.9993) with the correct first-year admissions page only at rank 3; the parking query pulls vetmed student handbooks at ranks 2-4; financial aid is clean (all finaid.vt.edu).
Sibling-program staleness: for the Data-Centric Computing query, 2019-2020 governance 'Supporting Docs' (proposal documents) outrank the current cs.vt.edu checksheets/roadmaps page (rank 2, 0.933).

Math program queries are strong on topical match (MathMajorHandbook / catalog mathematics-bs) but mix graduate pages into the verbose variant's top-5 (grad-policies.pdf, future-grads, graduate-program-presentation).

top_k 5 vs 12: top-5 yields 3-5 distinct documents, top-12 yields 7-12 (adds 4-7 docs). Selected text roughly 2.4x (e.g., 9,730 -> 23,062 chars), so the planned 24,000-char evidence budget is nearly exhausted at top-12 for checksheet-heavy queries.
Latency is not a constraint at candidate_k=30: mean 0.12s embed, 0.25s for three Qdrant queries, 0.29s to rerank <=30 passages — under 1s end-to-end per query through the port-forwards.
Dense/sparse agreement: 8-12 of each final top-12 also appear in the dense-only top-30 — RRF fusion rarely contradicts the dense branch; sparse mainly adds recall breadth.

Collections: hokiehelp-test (268,330 points, embed_version=2, named dense+sparse vectors) is what the live chatbot queries; hokiehelp-6898505471 (8,690 points, catalog.vt.edu course descriptions, no embed_version -> v1 body-only vectors) is a separate corpus not referenced by the live chatbot config.
access_notes: No cluster access failures: embeddings-service /embed, /rerank, /health and Qdrant read endpoints all reachable via kubectl port-forward (read-only usage; no writes, no index creation).
Branch retriever code as-is cannot run against the live collection (HTTP 400, unnamed vector) — documented under embedding_compatibility.checkout_mismatches.
search_many (candidate_k=30, global top_k=12, no neighbors) had not landed in the working tree at evaluation time; this probe mirrors those exact semantics against the live services instead.
